body:
i can confirm this is a problem and it does happen indeed.

@ia3andy ideas on why codestarts gets mixed up here?
We don't handle creating extensions for old streams, extensions templates are in the base codestarts, they are not platform dependent.

Any reason why not? 

In any case that does seem like a surprise to users and we should print a warning/provide info on what they should do instead.

> We don't handle creating extensions for old streams, extensions templates are in the base codestarts, they are not platform dependent.

I followed Quarkus CLI help (and didn't find note in quarkus.io docs)

```
[mvavrik@fedora ~]$ quarkus extension create --help | grep '\-stream' -A 2
  -S, --stream=platformKey:streamId
                         A target stream, for example:
                           io.quarkus.platform:2.0
```

It's very unlikely we end up with a similar breaking situation for extensions in the future (breaking import). 
The code is supposed to be working with all the streams (Quarkus 2-3 is an anomaly because of the change of imports).

Switching to Quarkus 2 from Quarkus 3 imports shouldn't be big deal and the way forward if people still want to create 2.xx extensions (or use a 2.x version of the CLI)

You are right @michalvavrik , we should remove the `stream` option from the `extension create` this is a bug.

I tend to disagree. You made all the base codestarts compatible with 2.x/3.x so I don't see why we wouldn't use the same trick for the extension codestart.
Granted you probably use the 2.13 CLI to create extensions for 2.13 but it doesn't cost us much to make sure it doesn't fail so let's be consistent and avoid the failure.

Also creating extensions for old versions perfectly makes sense in the context of RHBQ so let's not remove the option.

I will create a PR.

issue.title: Make sure all base codestarts work for 2.x and 3.x
